turn.user_message: Show me who is in charge
turn.context: Discharge sample conversation, turn 8 (playbook §4: the peak-load check on this hospital’s own pattern).

transcript.label: Sample conversation · turn 8 · who is in charge

text: You need one person to own discharge, and two people to run it day to day. Why:
bullets: Nobody owns the whole wait today, and your own numbers are past the lines where one owner is needed.
Two helpers, not three, because your work comes in two busy times of day, not spread across 24 hours.
Every other team only records and approves a little more. Their jobs do not change.
chat.invite: Last part: how we will know it worked.
chat.note: One owner, two helpers, sized to your busy hours.
prompts: Show me how we’ll know it worked
Can one of our nurses become the manager?
Our busy hours change at weekends
chat.pointer: Pick a role to open it. The two chains show why two helpers, not three.

blocks.title: One owner, two helpers
blocks.deck: The roles, then the two ways to size the helpers: the usual rule, and your busy hours.

roles.title: Discharge Manager
roles.line: Owns the whole process. About ₹4 to 4.5 lakh a year.

roles.title: Discharge Executives
roles.line: Look after each patient going home. About ₹3 to 3.5 lakh each.

roles.title: Everyone else
roles.line: Records and approves a little more. Same jobs.

steps.title: Two busy times a day
steps.line: The 7 PM round, then 11 AM to about 3 PM

steps.title: One helper for each
steps.line: Sized to the peak, not the day

blocks.caption: My working from your times. Check it against your staff rota before hiring.

sheets.title: Discharge Manager
sheets.text: One person answers for every delay, instead of each team blaming the process. Works with the bed desk manager as an equal.
sheets.entry: Could someone you have take this role?

sheets.title: Discharge Executives
sheets.text: They take over each patient from the evening round. They spot delays as they happen and chase the team holding things up.

lines.label: How many
lines.value: Two, one for each busy time

sheets.entry: When are your two busiest times?

sheets.title: Everyone else
sheets.text: Every other team only records and approves a little more. Their jobs do not change.
sheets.entry: Which team would feel this most?

blocks.label: New roles, cost a year
blocks.sub: One manager and two helpers. About 1% of what the waiting costs a year, worked out from your figures.
